column2: req_desc

Run manifest and health
Ship the run manifest and serve on the published port with a health check that reports whether file storage is reachable, as set out in Deployment and API.

Published settings
Read every setting in the settings table from its environment variable at boot, use its default when it is unset, and apply it on server time or page timers as each row states.

Grading routes
When grading is switched on, answer the seed, session, clock, operation batch and storage routes exactly as published, and answer 404 for each of them when it is off.

Accounts and sessions
Sign people up and in with a local username and password, keep them signed in with the session cookie for the session lifetime on server time, and limit sign-in attempts per username.

One error order
Every API error uses the one published body shape and code list and follows the one published precedence order.

Server boundary
Serve only the app's own assets from one origin, enforce the published body-size limits and security rules, and keep running when a dependency is unreachable at boot, as qualified in Server boundary.

Map list and templates
The map list shows the recent maps card trio and a grid of every map with a live miniature, and the New map dialog creates a blank map or one of the three published templates.

Dialogs, sheets and focus
Every dialog, sheet, drawer and menu keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside itself while open, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener, and once closed it is hidden and unreachable at every viewport.

Home page
The home page carries the home branch field, product statement line, shrinking top bar, feature split with checklist blocks and site footer in the published visual language.

Working screens look
The map list, editor, dialogs, notices and audience screen use the published palette roles, branch colours, type, corner rules and notice bands.

Wiring from the environment
Every service credential and URL is read from the environment at start, never hard-coded or sent to the browser, and every stored-object state comes from a real storage call.

Mind map layout
Topic boxes, wrapping, side balancing and coordinates in the mind map layout follow the published layout engine exactly, including both worked examples.

Topic keys
Tab, Enter, F2, typing, Escape and Delete create, rename and remove topics with the published focus results.

Arrow navigation
Arrow keys, Home and End move focus between topics by the published rules for each layout and side.

Map tree semantics
The map is an accessible tree with one focusable topic at a time, and each topic carries correct level, position, set size, expanded state and the published label grammar.

Keyboard moves and side pins
Alt+arrow keys reorder, demote, outdent and pin level 2 topics to a side as published, and each move is announced with the topic's new position.

Multi-select
Ctrl+click and Shift+ArrowUp or Shift+ArrowDown select several sibling topics, and moves and deletes act on all of them as one change and one undo.

Build a map by keyboard
An owner builds, renames, reorders and pins a whole map from the keyboard, ending with the published coordinates, focus and announcements.

Org chart, list and floating topics
The org chart and list layouts and floating topics follow the published layout engine exactly.

Regrow
A layout switch moves each visible topic from its old box to its new box with the published Regrow animations, along with the other published animations, and under reduced motion no animation runs.

Per-person collapse
Collapsing is saved for each person and map, removes hidden descendants from view, tab order, outline and accessibility tree, and never changes another person's view.

Cross-links and boundaries
Cross-links and boundaries always reference existing topics, draw to the nearest visible ancestor when their end is hidden, and follow moves, deletes and undo.

Viewport, focus branch and minimap
Zoom, pan, Fit to screen, Focus branch with its breadcrumb and deep link, and the minimap follow the published viewport rules.

Switch layouts together
Two co-editors switch layouts, collapse branches and focus a branch, and each screen shows the published coordinates, animations and per-person views.

Outline view
The outline is a second, live, two-way view of the same tree, edited with Tab, Shift+Tab and Enter by the published rules.

Find, filter and replace
Find in map searches titles and notes with a published match count, filters dim non-matching topics, and Replace all is one undoable change that skips locked topics.

Live sync and presence
Every change reaches every open screen through the live connection without reload, and presence shows each person with a published colour, cursor, selection ring and follow mode.

Outline and map together
Two people edit through the outline and the map at once, and both screens converge to the same tree with correct accessibility values and a one-step undo of a replace.

Operation log
Every change is an operation with an id and a base revision, applied in server order, refused when its base is too old, and returned unchanged when its id is resent.

Title merge
Concurrent edits of one title merge by character offset with the published tie-break, including inside an open title input, and match all four worked examples.

Work offline
Working offline queues changes that survive reload, shows the published banner, and on reconnect replays each change once and announces the published sent and conflict counts.

Session expiry
When a session passes its lifetime on server time, the Sign in again dialog opens, and unsent work and open text survive until the person signs in again.

Offline edits merge
Two people edit offline and reconnect in a known order, and both screens show the same merged map with the published conflict counts.

Move conflicts
Crossing moves that would make a cycle and two moves of one topic follow the published winner rules, and the losing editor sees a rollback, focus and notice as published.

Delete wins and Recovered edits
An edit inside a branch someone else deleted is set aside in Recovered edits with a notice, and it can be re-applied as a new topic.

Anchored reorder and locked groups
Sibling reorders follow their published anchors, and a change touching a locked topic is refused whole with the published notice.

Resolve crossing edits
Two co-editors make crossing moves, a delete under an open edit and competing reorders, and both screens end on the same tree with the published notices and focus.

Personal undo and redo
Undo and redo reverse only the acting person's own changes, are kept on the server per person and map, and skip a change someone else has since touched, as published.

Undo of a delete
Undoing a delete brings back the whole branch with the same ids, comments, votes, attachments, cross-links and boundaries at its old place.

Activity
The Activity panel lists every change with its published sentence, newest first, filterable by person, and selecting a row focuses its topic.

Undo around co-editors
A co-editor undoes and redoes around another person's edits and a deleted branch, and the results, notices and stack survive reload.

Published breakpoints
The editor and the other screens show their published arrangement at phone, tablet and desk widths with no horizontal overflow.

Touch gestures
Tap, long press, drag to reparent with a drop preview and edge panning, one-finger pan and two-finger pinch follow the published touch rules.

Phone topic sheet
On a phone, topic details open as a bottom sheet with Notes, Task and Comments tabs, and the long-press menu offers the published actions.

Edit on a phone
A co-editor edits a map by touch on a phone while a desktop co-editor watches the same changes arrive live.

Versions and playback
Automatic and named versions are cut as published, and the playback slider and read-only version view show any version.

Version diff
Comparing two versions reports added, removed, moved and edited topics by the published id rules and marks each topic.

Version restore
Only the owner restores a version, which comes back exactly as a new undoable change and a new version, seen live by everyone, as qualified in Business rules.

Replay and restore history
An owner replays, compares and restores history while a second person watches, then undoes the restore.

Slides and presenter view
The owner orders slides by keyboard, presents with a live follower count and speaker notes, and deleted or restricted slides are skipped with the published notices.

Presentation camera
Each presentation step moves the camera with the published animation to frame the slide's branch by the fit rule, and under reduced motion it cuts straight there.

Audience session states
The audience screen shows waiting, live, paused or ended from the server's session state alone, follows steps live, and lets a phone swipe back to earlier slides.

Present to an audience
An owner presents to an audience member on a phone through a waiting, live, paused and ended session with slides deleted mid-show and edits appearing live.

Roles and live role changes
The server enforces the published permission table for owner, editor, commenter and viewer, and a role change or removal takes effect live on the affected screen.

Branch locks
Branch locks are inherited by descendants, shown on each topic, and refuse edits from everyone except the locker and the owner on the server.

Share links
Share links grant exactly one role on one map, expire at their server-recorded instant, die when revoked or regenerated, and end sessions opened through them live.

Restricted branches
A restricted branch is absent for commenters, viewers, guests and the audience in every view, count, export, diff, slide and API answer.

Share and restrict a map
An owner shares, downgrades, revokes, locks and restricts while a second person's screen follows each change live.

Task rollups
Task progress, earliest due date and overdue state roll up through ancestors by the published rules and update live on every screen after any change.

Dependencies
Depends-on links block a topic until its target is done or cancelled, refuse loops, and keep blocked counts current after any change.

Style cascade and themes
Colour, shape and text colour follow the published cascade, the three themes and the luminance rule, and moving a branch recalculates every inherited value.

Large maps
From the published size, only topics near the view are in the page, within the published ceiling, while keyboard focus and accessibility values stay correct for the whole tree.

Track progress on a large map
Two people move, undo and tick tasks on a large map, and both screens show the published rollups, blocked counts and colours.

Comments and mentions
Topics carry threaded comments with one level of replies, @mentions and a live inbox, and threads resolve and reopen.

Votes and counts
Star votes, comment counts and every other topic count always equal their recomputed values after moves, deletes, replay, undo and restore.

Safe notes
Topic notes render only the published markdown subset, refuse links outside the published schemes, and never run script from anyone's text.

Discuss topics
A commenter and an editor discuss topics with mentions and votes, and everything follows a moved topic and survives a delete and its undo.

Sprig outline format
Imports and exports use the published Sprig outline format, with exact line errors, and round-trip canonical input byte for byte.

Import preview and branch paste
An uploaded outline is stored first, previewed, then grafted under a chosen topic as one undoable change, and branches copy and paste between maps by the published rules.

Export jobs
An export is a background job with live published progress, and its download is offered only after the stored object exists.

Image attachments
An image attachment is checked for size, content type and the per-map quota in the published order, and it counts as attached only after storage confirms it.

Storage outage
When file storage is down, at boot or later, maps stay editable, every storage action shows its published outage copy, and everything recovers without a restart.

Import, export and attach
An editor imports, previews, grafts, pastes, exports and attaches through a storage outage and its recovery, and every file exists in storage before the screen says so.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve fields and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and those commands alone install, build and serve the app.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json, plus the bundled Figtree font files) with its licence.
Every shipped package is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or Unlicense, and the bundled fonts are under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
The app uses no datastore other than the given PostgreSQL database and object store bucket: no SQLite, no files written as a database, and no in-memory store standing in for durable state.
The browser makes no request to any origin but the app's own: no font, icon, script, image or analytics from elsewhere.
The provided service configuration and environment files are left unchanged.
The app registers no service worker.
The database schema is applied idempotently each time the app serves, not only at build.
